items.title: Safety, Signal Quality, and Patient Satisfaction With Insertable Loop Recorder Implantation by Specialized Electrophysiology Nurses: Prospective Observational Study.
items.abstract: Insertable loop recorders (ILRs) are subcutaneous cardiac monitoring devices used in the diagnosis of arrhythmias and in the etiological investigation of syncope and cryptogenic stroke. Device miniaturization and procedural simplification have facilitated implantation in ambulatory settings. The involvement of specialized electrophysiology nurses may help meet rising clinical demand, although evidence in our setting remains limited. This study aimed to analyze implantation safety, detection signal quality, adverse events during follow-up, and patient satisfaction when the procedure was performed by specialized nurses. This prospective observational study (the CARDIONURSE study) was conducted in the Arrhythmia Unit of Hospital General Universitario Doctor Balmis between February 2022 and May 2023. Thirty-five patients with a clinical indication for ILR implantation were included. The procedure was performed by 2 specialized nurses under medical supervision. Sociodemographic, clinical, and technical implantation variables were collected, including detection signal amplitude (mV), together with adverse events and follow-up outcomes at 1 and 6 months. Patient satisfaction was assessed using a study-specific questionnaire at 4 time points. Descriptive statistical analysis was performed. Mean age was 71.1 (SD 11.3) years, and 62.9% (22/35) were women. The most frequent indication was syncope (27/35, 77.1%), followed by suspected atrial fibrillation (AF) in cryptogenic stroke (6/35, 17.1%). No objective procedural complications occurred (35/35, 100% of procedures); mild, transient procedural pain was reported in 5.7% (2/35) of patients, and the procedure lasted less than 5 minutes in 74.3% (26/35) of procedures. Mean signal amplitude was 0.45 (SD 0.29) mV, with a visible P wave in 94.3% (33/35) of patients. No wound-related adverse events were recorded among the 85.7% (30/35) of patients with available follow-up data at 6 months; data were unavailable for the remaining 5 patients. A diagnosis was obtained in 20% (6/30) of patients with an available diagnostic outcome at 6 months. Overall, 97.1% (34/35) of patients reported maximum or very high satisfaction with the intervention, and 100% (35/35) with the care received. ILR implantation by specialized electrophysiology nurses in an ambulatory setting is a safe, fast, and technically adequate procedure, with adequate signal quality and high patient satisfaction. These findings support the feasibility of specialized nursing as ILR implanters in similar ambulatory care settings, although confirmation in larger, multicenter studies is warranted before broader implementation.

items.title: Experimental protocol for the application of multiphoton endoscopy to image biological tissues.
items.abstract: Multiphoton endoscopy has emerged as a promising extension of multiphoton microscopy, enabled by recent advances in nonlinear fiber optics. By combining optical sectioning, intrinsic contrast mechanisms, and flexible probe geometries, multiphoton endoscopy enables imaging in confined or nontraditional environments that are inaccessible to conventional benchtop systems. However, practical implementation remains challenging due to constraints imposed by probe miniaturization, scanning nonuniformity, and sample-dependent photodamage. Here, we present a practical multiphoton endoscopy protocol applying a commercially available, miniaturized two-photon endoscopic system. We describe system configuration, calibration procedures, and imaging strategies with a particular focus on spiral scan calibration and laser power ramping to compensate for non-uniform excitation across the field of view. The protocol is validated across a diverse set of reference materials and biological samples, including autofluorescent standards, three-dimensional smooth muscle cell constructs, rodent and human vascular tissues, brain sections, and plant leaves, involving both labeled and label-free imaging modalities. We discuss common pitfalls, limitations, and troubleshooting strategies encountered during routine operation, including photobleaching in thin histological sections and constraints arising from fixed excitation wavelength. Together, this work provides a practical guide for implementing multiphoton endoscopy in experimental settings and highlights key considerations for adapting the technique to a broad range of biological applications.
authors: Sophie M L van de Walle
Marc A M J van Zandvoort

items.title: Descriptive histological study of the sympathetic innervation of the human internal thoracic artery as a pedicle and a skeletonized graft.
items.abstract: The internal thoracic artery is an important graft used in coronary artery bypass surgery. However, there is a debate on the best practice regarding harvest, i.e., skeletonized or pedicled preparation. It remains controversial how skeletonization affects internal thoracic artery innervation. The presented exploratory study aimed to complement previous studies with a detailed histomorphological and histomorphometric analysis of the bilateral structure of the internal thoracic artery wall and innervation after skeletonized and pedicled preparation. Overall, 25 nitrite pickling salt and ethanol fixed corpses were included in the study. The left and right internal thoracic artery samples were both skeletonized and pedicled and divided into a proximal and a distal segment. Hematoxylin-eosin and Elastica van Gieson stains, and S100-, calcitonin gene-related peptide-, and tyrosine hydroxylase-immunolabeling were used to histomorphologically and histomorphometrically assess the samples. Explorative statistical analyses including age, sex, and the hierarchical data structure were computed. No significant atherosclerotic changes were observed in the intimal layer in any of the specimens. A relevant portion, i.e., 11/25 left and 13/25 right internal thoracic artery samples, presented with alterations of at least 50% of the tunica media assessed. No indication for a relevant impact of age and sex on the analyses of interest was found. As compared to pedicled vessels, skeletonized vessels showed a drastically reduced number of nerves accompanying the vessel. A great portion of the nerves following the internal thoracic artery was tyrosine hydrolase-immunoreactive. In summary, the histology-centered analyzes showed that skeletonization impacts internal thoracic artery innervation by drastically reducing the number of nerves accompanying the vessel. The analysis further revealed that internal thoracic artery medial degeneration is a frequent observation in elderly individuals. Further studies are needed to determine the impact of medial degeneration and hampered innervation on graft function.

items.title: Advances in obstetric anesthesia care in patients with severe cardiac comorbidities.
items.abstract: This review aims to update the reader about recent clinical practice recommendations in caring for the cardio-obstetric patient. The emergence of pregnancy heart teams has facilitated multidisciplinary communication for caring for a pregnant patient with cardiac disease. The utilization of noninvasive diagnostic modalities such as brain natriuretic peptide and bedside transthoracic echocardiography can yield quick actionable results regarding therapeutic options. Vaginal delivery remains the preferred mode of delivery for the vast majority of pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease. Timely and effective use of mechanical circulatory support in pregnancy can be beneficial for patients in cardiogenic shock or decompensated heart failure. Anesthesiologists are essential team members within the pregnancy heart team and should familiarize themselves with the evidence-based guidelines for caring for pregnant patients with cardiac disease.

items.title: Joint associations of self-reported restless sleep and depressive symptoms with incident heart disease in older adults: A pooled analysis of 3 prospective cohort studies.
items.abstract: Restless sleep is an item on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression (CES-D) scale, so adjusting for a CES-D score partly adjusts for the exposure. Whether sleep complaints are associated with cardiovascular risk independently of depressive symptoms is unclear. We aim to examine separate and joint associations of restless sleep and depressive symptoms with incident heart disease in older adults. We analyzed 18,362 adults aged ≥60 years without reported heart disease from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, the Health and Retirement Study (United States), and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. The baseline CES-D item defined restless sleep and was removed from the depressive-symptom score. Incident heart disease was a self-reported physician diagnosis at later waves. Cohort-specific weighted grouped-time proportional hazards estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis. Over 171,863 person-years, 4906 participants reported incident heart disease. Relative to neither condition, pooled hazard ratios were 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.98-1.16) for restless sleep alone, 1.16 (1.03-1.31) for depressive symptoms alone, and 1.36 (1.20-1.55) for both. The both-conditions estimate was significant in each cohort and similar in most post hoc sensitivity analyses. The estimate for depressive symptoms alone and the contrast between both conditions and depressive symptoms alone were not stable to cohort omission. No clear departure from additivity was detected. In an exploratory analysis restricted to participants without elevated depressive symptoms at 2 assessments 2 years apart, restless sleep reported at both assessments was not clearly associated with incident heart disease (1.15, 95% CI 0.96-1.37). At 7 to 8 years, standardized risk (death treated as censoring) was 4.0 to 7.5 percentage points higher with both conditions than neither. Restless sleep without elevated depressive symptoms was not clearly associated with incident heart disease, whereas its combination with elevated depressive symptoms identified a higher-risk group in every cohort, without evidence of synergy. An independent contribution of restless sleep beyond depressive symptoms was not established. In later life, restless sleep should be interpreted together with depressive symptoms rather than on its own.

items.title: A Mixed-Method Analysis of How Misinformation and Disinformation in Social Media and Personal Networks Affects Vaccine Hesitancy Among Older Adults.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study examines how exposure to false or misleading information-whether unintentional (misinformation) or deliberate (disinformation)- through social media and other networks may shape vaccination decisions among older adults.MethodsFocusing on participants 55 and older obtained from the COVID-19 Coping Study, we used logistic regression to analyze use of health information sources (i.e. social media, news, family and friends) adjusted by region, race, age category and gender among the unvaccinated. We used thematic analysis to group responses on why they were unvaccinated into misinformation, disinformation and other.ResultsUnvaccinated participants were 3.2 times more likely to have received health information from family and friends and 3.5 times more likely to have received information through e-mail or message boards. Among respondents who had not received the COVID vaccine, misinformation and disinformation were prominent in shaping vaccine hesitancy.ConclusionTargeted interventions and community-led strategies may show promise in mitigating negative effects.
items.journal: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing

items.title: Assessment of Immunotherapy Response by Analyzing Tumor Microenvironment Alterations in Advanced Gastric Cancer: A Study Protocol.
items.abstract: IntroductionAdvanced gastric cancer has a poor prognosis, and reliable biomarkers for identifying patients who may benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) combined with chemotherapy remain limited. Dynamic alterations in the tumor microenvironment (TME) may provide clinically useful information regarding treatment response. This study aims to investigate longitudinal TME changes in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving ICIs plus chemotherapy and to explore their associations with treatment response.MethodsThis is a prospective, single-center biomarker study in patients with advanced gastric cancer receiving ICIs plus chemotherapy. Matched tumor tissue samples from primary and/or metastatic lesions, together with peripheral blood samples, will be collected before treatment and after four cycles of combination therapy. Patients achieving complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) will be classified as the high-response group (HRG), whereas patients with progressive disease (PD) will be classified as the non-response group (NRG). Pre- and post-treatment TME alterations will be analyzed within each patient, and differences between the HRG and NRG will be compared, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), H3K4me3, cytokines, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and tumor markers. Associations with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), mismatch repair (MMR), and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA (EBER) status will also be explored.ConclusionsThis study may identify dynamic TME-related biomarkers associated with response to ICIs combined with chemotherapy, and may provide evidence for future response-stratification strategies in advanced gastric cancer. Advanced gastric cancer is difficult to treat, and not all patients benefit from immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy. This study will investigate whether changes in the environment surrounding gastric cancer cells can help identify patients who are more likely to respond to treatment. Tumor tissue and blood samples will be collected before treatment and after four treatment cycles. The study will compare changes in immune cells, selected proteins, inflammatory markers, and tumor markers between patients who respond well and those whose cancer progresses. The aim is to identify potential markers that may help doctors better understand treatment response in the future. This is an exploratory study, and any promising findings will need to be confirmed in larger studies.
items.journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center

items.title: Ivermectin and dendritic cell function: insights into inflammatory and anti-inflammatory dynamics.
items.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) regulate T cell-mediated immunity and are potential targets for cancer immunotherapy. The direct effects of ivermectin (IVM), an antiparasitic drug with reported immunomodulatory properties, on human monocyte-derived DCs remain unclear. This study examined whether IVM alters the surface phenotype and expression of inflammatory and regulatory genes in these cells. DCs were generated from human peripheral blood monocytes, treated with a nontoxic concentration of IVM, and stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Surface marker expression was assessed by flow cytometry, and transcript levels were measured by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Compared with control DCs cultured without IVM, IVM-treated DCs showed higher surface expression of the co-stimulatory molecule CD86 and lower expression of CD11c and HLA-DR. Transcript levels of interleukin-12, interleukin-10, and tumor necrosis factor-α increased, whereas those of arginase 1, transforming growth factor-β, and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase decreased. IVM altered both inflammatory and regulatory features of human monocyte-derived DCs. The increase in CD86 alongside reduced HLA-DR expression and higher interleukin-10 transcript levels leaves the net effect on T cell activation unresolved. Functional studies are needed to assess how IVM-treated DCs influence T cell responses in vitro and whether these changes affect antitumor immunity in vivo .

items.title: Metastatic G2 laryngeal neuroendocrine tumor treated with sulfatinib and sintilimab: A case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Laryngeal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies with limited evidence guiding the management of metastatic disease. We report a metastatic G2 laryngeal NET initially presenting as an unusual temporal subcutaneous metastasis and subsequently treated with combined targeted therapy and immunotherapy. A 63-year-old man with a history of invasive lung adenocarcinoma presented with a 1.3 × 1.2 cm left temporal subcutaneous nodule and a history of hoarseness accompanied by throat pain. Histopathological examination of the temporal lesion suggested metastatic NET. Subsequent PET-CT, laryngoscopy, and biopsy identified a primary laryngeal NET. After vertical partial laryngectomy, right neck dissection, and laryngeal function reconstruction, pathology confirmed a well-differentiated G2 NET with cervical lymph-node and temporal subcutaneous metastases, classified as pT2N1M1, stage IVC. In March 2025, hepatic metastases were pathologically confirmed. Molecular profiling identified HRAS p.Q61L, KDR p.S265L, and ROS1 p.S615Y variants, microsatellite instability-high status, and programmed death-ligand 1expression with a combined positive score of 70. Combination therapy with sulfatinib (300 mg/day) and sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks) was initiated in April 2025 and continued without dose reduction, interruption, or delay. After 10 months of combination therapy, contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a reduction in the size of hepatic metastatic lesions compared with baseline, together with a marked decrease in the number of metastatic lesions. The largest index hepatic lesion decreased from 32.68 mm to 19.05 mm in maximal diameter, corresponding to a 41.7% reduction, demonstrating a marked radiological reduction in hepatic metastatic burden. At the latest documented assessment in February 2026, no further disease progression or treatment-related adverse events were observed. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of metastatic laryngeal NET with an unusual subcutaneous presentation. Comprehensive pathological and molecular evaluation may aid treatment decision-making in advanced disease. The observed disease control with sulfatinib plus sintilimab is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in additional patients.

items.title: Self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination: An exploratory cross-sectional survey in Egypt.
items.abstract: Peripheral neurological manifestations have been reported following Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection, whereas neuropathic symptoms after COVID-19 vaccination remain less well characterized. To evaluate self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination and identify factors associated with postvaccination symptom reporting, while accounting for previous confirmed COVID-19 infection. This cross-sectional survey included adults recruited from university-affiliated settings. Data were collected using a structured English/Arabic questionnaire covering COVID-19 infection, vaccination history, comorbidities, medication use, and neuropathic symptoms, including tingling, numbness, burning sensation, and electric shock-like sensations. Participants who reported symptoms were invited for neurological clinical assessment. The primary outcome was self-reported neuropathic symptoms potentially suggestive of peripheral neuropathy following COVID-19 vaccination. Previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was treated as a potential confounder in multivariable analysis. A total of 1201 individuals were screened, of whom 1166 were included in the final analysis. Postvaccination self-reported neuropathic symptoms were reported by 472 of 1090 vaccinated participants (43.3%). Following the first vaccine dose, symptom reporting differed significantly by vaccine type (P < .001), with the highest proportions observed among recipients of Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (190/316 [60.1%]) and Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine (37/92 [40.2%]). In multivariable analysis, older age, use of medications with reported or potential associations with peripheral neuropathy, and receipt of ChAdOx1-S, Gam-COVID-Vac, or Sinovac-CoronaVac were associated with increased post-vaccination symptom reporting (P < .05), whereas previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was not independently associated with the outcome. In exploratory booster-dose analysis, homologous booster vaccination was associated with lower odds of symptom reporting than heterologous boosting (adjusted odds ratio 0.38, P < .001). Self-reported neuropathic symptoms were frequently reported following COVID-19 vaccination and varied according to vaccine type. Older age, selected vaccine types, and heterologous booster schedules were associated with symptom reporting. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously because they reflect self-reported symptoms rather than confirmed peripheral neuropathy diagnoses and were not routinely confirmed by objective neurological investigations.

items.title: Infectious Disease Diagnostic Capacity Across Hospital Tiers in China: National Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.abstract: China's notifiable infectious disease surveillance relies on clinical recognition and diagnostic testing, but uneven hospital capacity may affect case ascertainment and interpretation of reported burden. This study aims to assess infectious disease diagnostic capacity across hospital tiers in China, including alignment with notified disease burden, regional variation, diagnostic modalities, and implementation barriers. We conducted a national cross-sectional web-based survey of hospitals in China in 2023. After centralized quality control and eligibility screening, 2689 hospitals were included: 124 (4.6%) primary, 1478 (55%) secondary, and 1087 (40.4%) tertiary hospitals. We assessed in-house and send-out testing availability; compared diagnostic availability with national notified incidence and mortality; and examined regional variation, selected diagnostic modalities, and reported barriers. Median in-house diagnostic coverage increased from 11.6% (IQR 9.3%-18.6%) in primary hospitals to 27.9% (IQR 18.6%-37.2%) in secondary hospitals and 39.5% (IQR 27.9%-48.8%) in tertiary hospitals; corresponding overall coverage, including send-out testing, was 14% (IQR 9.3%-23.3%), 32.6% (IQR 23.3%-44.2%), and 44.2% (IQR 30.2%-55.8%), respectively. Tier differences persisted in sensitivity analyses. Diagnostic availability was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. In-house hepatitis B testing was available in 82.3% (102/124), 98% (1449/1478), and 99.3% (1079/1087) of primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals, respectively. Pulmonary tuberculosis showed a pronounced tier gradient (26/124, 21% in primary vs 910/1087, 83.7% in tertiary hospitals). Hand, foot, and mouth disease and other infectious diarrheal diseases had limited availability even in tertiary hospitals (380/1087, 35% and 456/1087, 42%, respectively) despite high incidence. Some lower-incidence but high-consequence infections also had limited local capacity, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (151/1087, 13.9%) and rabies (43/1087, 4%) in tertiary hospitals. Geographic variation was partly consistent with known disease endemicity, with higher testing availability for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in northeastern hospitals, although only 35.9% (55/153) of tertiary hospitals in this region offered in-house testing. Diagnostic depth also varied across tiers: hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA testing increased from 8.1% (10/124) in primary hospitals to 61.1% (664/1087) in tertiary hospitals. For COVID-19, primary hospitals more frequently reported antigen than nucleic acid testing (57/124, 46% vs 27/124, 21.8%). Lower-tier hospitals more often reported workforce and infrastructure constraints, whereas tertiary hospitals more frequently cited reagent-licensing and fee-schedule barriers. Among surveyed hospitals, infectious disease diagnostic capacity differed substantially across hospital tiers, varied geographically, and was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. These disparities extended beyond disease coverage to specific testing modalities and barriers to capacity expansion. These findings support tiered, regionally responsive diagnostic networks that provide essential testing closer to first-contact care while ensuring timely access to specialized diagnostics through reliable, quality-assured referral pathways.

items.title: Rapid growth of amphetamine use among treatment-seeking individuals with substance use disorders in Oman, 2019-2024: a retrospective descriptive and analytical study.
items.abstract: Background: In Oman, emerging post-COVID-19 reports suggest a substantial shift in substance use patterns, particularly toward stimulant use among individuals seeking addiction treatment. Objectives: We analyzed substance use patterns among treatment-seeking individuals with substance use disorders (SUDs) using pooled National Registry for Addiction data from 2019 to 2024 and identified factors associated with amphetamine use. Methods: A retrospective descriptive and analytical study was conducted using anonymized registry data. Sociodemographic characteristics, substance use patterns, routes of administration, and blood-borne infections were analyzed among 2,902 individuals. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with amphetamine use. Results: The study population was predominantly male (97.7%), young (mean age 33 ± 9 years), and Omani (98.4%). Opiates and cannabis were reported by 71.5% and 59.9% of individuals, respectively. Stimulant use increased sharply from 8% in 2019 to 66% in 2024. Injection drug use was reported by 66.0% of individuals; after adjustment for other substances, opiate use remained the dominant category associated with injection drug use, accounting for approximately 81.8% of IDU cases. In multivariable analysis, younger age (aOR = 0.96, 95% CI [0.95, 0.97], p   p  = .006), intermediate education (aOR = 1.28, 95% CI [1.05, 1.55], p  = .014), and unemployment (aOR = 2.36, 95% CI [1.99, 2.79], p   Conclusions: Among treatment-seeking individuals in Oman, substance use patterns shifted rapidly toward stimulants, consistent with regional and global ATS trends, supporting strengthened surveillance and targeted prevention.
items.journal: The American journal of drug and alcohol abuse

items.title: Exploring barriers and facilitators to Hepatitis C virus treatment access in Los Angeles County: A mixed-methods study.
items.abstract: Diagnosed but untreated chronic Hepatitis C virus infection remains an important public health problem in Los Angeles County, particularly affecting underserved and minority groups. This mixed-methods study (October 2024-January 2025) aimed to identify and describe the barriers and facilitators to accessing Hepatitis C virus treatment among Los Angeles County residents. The study used de-identified programmatic data from 344 case-residents in a linkage-to-cure program and conducted thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with ten participants (seven untreated, three treated) from the linkage-to-cure program. Overall, 54% of case-residents reported experiencing barriers. Among those reporting specific barriers (n = 91), personal barriers were most common (43%), followed by provider-related barriers (31%), insurance barriers (13%), and inadequate access to medical care (13%). Interviews provided further context. Themes identified included homelessness, incarceration, and drug addiction as key personal barriers. Provider-related barriers included language barriers, expressed frustration in navigating the healthcare system, long wait times to see a provider, and participants' lack of HCV information. Insurance barriers were characterized by cost barriers and inadequate access to medical care due to a lack of transportation. Facilitators of treatment access included personal motivation to seek treatment, family and community-based support systems, trust in their medical provider, adequate insurance coverage, understanding the benefits of HCV treatment, and the desire to avoid stigmatization. Local efforts to eliminate Hepatitis C should consider equitable interventions that address individual and system-level barriers. Potential strategies include implementing language support services, leveraging patient navigation and care coordination services, utilizing mobile clinics for the unhoused, ensuring treatment continuity for people re-entering the community from incarceration, and removing insurance restrictions, such as prior authorization requirements.

items.title: Provider knowledge and prescribing practices of HIV PrEP, PEP and PEP-in-pocket among women in Canada: A cross-sectional study of healthcare providers.
items.abstract: Women represent an increasing, yet underserved proportion of people living with HIV in Canada. Biomedical prevention strategies, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), and PEP-in-pocket (PIP), are recommended in national guidelines but are not routinely implemented in women's care. This study evaluated Canadian healthcare provider knowledge, willingness, and prescribing practices for PrEP, PEP, and PIP. Eligible providers completed an online survey assessing demographics, HIV knowledge, prescribing practices, and perceptions of gender-related differences in prophylaxis delivery. A total of 114 responses were included in the analysis. While providers reported generally high knowledge of HIV, familiarity with medication-based prevention was more variable. Most respondents reported conditional willingness to prescribe PrEP and PEP (PrEP: 57.4%; PEP: 71.4%), with fewer reporting proactive prescribing (PEP: 25.0%; PrEP 25.9%), or avoidance (PEP: 3.6%; PrEP 16.7%). Despite 74% reporting familiarity with PEP, half referred patients to the emergency department or other providers for initiation, potentially delaying access within the 72-hour window. Prescribing practices were skewed towards men, with 67% of providers more likely to initiate HIV prevention discussions with men. Key barriers included insufficient knowledge, perceived lower risk for women, stigma, and lack of validated screening tools. Women's Health and Obstetrics and Gynecology (OB/GYN) providers reported the lowest familiarity and highest prescribing avoidance, with 81% and 88% reporting never prescribing PrEP or PEP, respectively. Familiarity with PIP was limited, with 56% overall and 88% of Women's Health and OB/GYN providers reporting no familiarity. Nurse Practitioners demonstrated higher proactive PrEP prescribing and no PEP avoidance, suggesting a role for nurse-led models. These findings highlight a persistent gap between knowledge and implementation of HIV prophylaxis for women in Canada. Addressing provider-level knowledge, prescribing confidence, and structural barriers will be critical to ensure equitable access to PrEP, PEP and PIP.

items.title: Update in alternative donor strategies in heart and lung transplantation.
items.abstract: Alternative donor strategies in cardiothoracic transplantation are becoming routine. This review covers recent developments and their implications for the anesthesiologist. Donor scarcity is a principal constraint on heart and lung transplantation. Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and the adoption of machine preservation have reshaped the donor pool. This review covers literature comparing thoracoabdominal normothermic regional perfusion with direct procurement and preservation, warm ischemic thresholds and their relationship to primary graft dysfunction, normothermic and hypothermic ex-situ perfusion, 10 °C static cold storage, and ex-vivo lung perfusion, and discusses the ethics of DCD. Extended-criteria and hepatitis C virus-viremic donors are now used routinely, and cardiac xenotransplantation is entering clinical study. Each advance alters graft physiology at reperfusion and the timing of perioperative services. Research into cardiac xenotransplantation is ongoing. These strategies enlarge the donor pool and introduce novel graft physiological concerns, as well as ethical concerns, for the anesthesiologist.

items.title: CD36 + Kupffer cells control postprandial lipid clearance and fuel metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver diseases.
items.abstract: Liver macrophages comprise distinct populations with specialized functions. Kupffer cells (KCs) populate liver sinusoids during embryonic development and monitor the blood, clear erythrocytes, and recycle iron. In metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), KCs acquire a lipid-associated macrophage phenotype characterized by the expression of CD36. Whether lipid-associated KCs exist at steady state and perform physiological functions remains unclear. Here, we show that CD36 + KCs, previously identified as KC2, are present at steady state in both mice and healthy human livers and that lipid handling is an intrinsic feature of this KC subset. Using KC-specific Cd36 deletion, we demonstrate that CD36 is required for postprandial hepatic lipid retention in healthy mice. CD36 + KCs also promoted lipid accumulation during MASLD, whereas KC-specific CD36 deficiency attenuated hepatic steatosis, identifying this subset as a regulator of physiological lipid homeostasis and metabolic liver disease.

items.title: Global burden of HBV/HCV-related liver diseases, 1990-2021, and projections to 2050: A global burden of disease study 2021.
items.abstract: Despite the availability of measures to control hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related diseases, achieving elimination remains a substantial challenge. Effective action demands accurate assessment of the present and anticipation of the future. We utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2021 to estimate the global burden of HBV- and HCV-related diseases for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We defined HBV/HCV-related liver disease to include chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and cirrhosis attributable to chronic HBV or HCV. The burden was assessed using the age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), stratified by region, age, sex, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI). GBD estimates were reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs); 1990 to 2021 percentage changes were calculated from point estimates. Forecasting analysis was conducted using the GBD 2021 forecast framework, supplemented by Das Gupta decomposition analysis. From 1990 to 2021, the global ASMRs of HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis declined by 41.51% and 31.47%, respectively, while liver cancer-related ASMR showed divergent changes (HBV: -16.40%; HCV: +2.35%). ASDRs also declined across both cirrhosis and liver cancer (HBV: -42.07%, -22.34%; HCV: -29.34%, -8.24%). Regionally, the highest ASMRs for chronic hepatitis B and C including cirrhosis in 2021 were observed in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa (14.51 per 1,00,000) and Central Sub-Saharan Africa (13.92 per 1,00,000), respectively. The burden of both viruses was generally higher in men. Age-specific mortality rates were highest in older age groups across HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases. By the late 2030s, the mortality burden of chronic hepatitis C is projected to surpass that of chronic hepatitis B, amid a slowing annual decline in the ASMR of chronic hepatitis C (-1.21% to -0.24%). Although the overall burden of HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases may decrease or stabilize, sustained progress hinges on equitable access to vaccination, optimized antiviral therapies, and a renewed global focus on HCV as its relative impact grows. Achieving meaningful reductions across SDI contexts will require not only scientific advances but also strategic efforts to improve affordability and distribution, supported by the political will to implement change.

items.title: Nomogram for predicting cancer-specific survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving chemotherapy.
items.abstract: Chemotherapy is 1 of the treatment options for patients with intermediate- and advanced-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and there is currently a lack of survival prediction models following chemotherapy. Our study aims to develop a nomogram to predict cancer-specific survival (CSS) in HCC patients following chemotherapy. A retrospective analysis was conducted using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database for 4150 HCC patients following chemotherapy between 2010 and 2019. Patients were randomly allocated in a 7:3 ratio to training and validation cohorts. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was employed to identify prognostic factors for nomogram construction. We utilized the concordance index (C-index), area under the curve values, calibration curves, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement to evaluate the performance and clinical value of the nomogram. The median age of all patients was 64 (interquartile range: 58-70) years, with 78.9% male. Six predictors were retained in the multivariable Cox model and used to construct the model. The C-index was 0.734 in the training cohort and 0.735 in the validation cohort. In both cohorts, the area under the curve values at 1, 3, and 5 years exceeded 0.78. Calibration curves demonstrated good consistency between the observed values and the nomogram predictions for CSS. Notably, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement suggested that the nomogram provided incremental predictive value beyond the American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system. Furthermore, we established a risk classification system capable of effectively stratifying patients into distinct risk groups. We developed and validated a nomogram that complements the American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system for predicting CSS in HCC patients receiving chemotherapy.

items.title: Acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy in metastatic wild-type RAS colorectal cancer: A CARE-compliant 2-case report.
items.abstract: Anti-EGFR therapy improves outcomes in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), but acquired resistance frequently emerges, and its mechanisms are heterogeneous. This report describes 2 patients with RAS wild-type mCRC who developed acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy. Both patients had RAS wild-type mCRC with multiple liver metastases and received cetuximab-based therapy as first-line treatment. Each patient experienced disease progression during treatment. Case 1: a Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog exon 2 codon 12 mutation was detected in a liver metastasis at the time of progression, whereas the primary tumor remained RAS wild-type. Case 2: human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) overexpression (immunohistochemistry 3+) was identified in the primary tumor on molecular reassessment after progression. Case 1 received cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 followed by cetuximab-based maintenance; after progression, molecular analysis of the liver metastasis detected a Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog mutation, anti-EGFR therapy was discontinued and switched to FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab, and the patient subsequently underwent liver metastasectomy, with quarterly liquid biopsies for monitoring. Case 2 received cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 followed by cetuximab plus 5-fluorouracil; after HER2 amplification was confirmed, treatment was switched to trastuzumab plus pertuzumab combined with chemotherapy, and surgery was deferred. At the last follow-up, case 1 had stable disease with undetectable RAS-mutated circulating tumor DNA after metastasectomy and continued chemotherapy. Case 2 showed gradual disease progression despite HER2-directed therapy and required further-line treatment. These 2 cases illustrate that acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy is a dynamic and heterogeneous process rather than a single event, and they support repeated molecular profiling of metastatic lesions to guide subsequent treatment selection.
